text:
Jules: quick heads-up — after bringing up the new reranker (llama3-rank-v2) on the holdout set we see a ~3.5% drop in NDCG@10 vs baseline. MRR mostly flat. run command I used:```./eval_harness --model llama3-rank-v2 --candidates holdout.jsonl --metrics ndcg@10,mrr --seed 42 --batch 256``` anyone seen this shape before?
Ravi: how big is the holdout exactly? 3.5% relative or absolute? :thinking_face:
Jules: 100k queries, 3.5% relative (baseline ndcg@10=0.422 -> new=0.407). rolled average across slices looks worse on head queries oddly.
Marta: can you dump per-query delta distribution? overall numbers hide a long-tail effect. a handful of queries with big negatives could explain it.
Jules: yeah warming up a run to spit per-query deltas now. also noticed we truncated docs to 512 tokens for the new model (baseline used 1024). could that be the culprit?
Ivy: truncation mismatch would definitely bias toward shorter docs. are we using the same tokenizer and token counting logic as baseline? sometimes byte-level vs wp changes where truncation cuts off.
Sam: also check candidate ordering in the eval harness. if candidate shuffle happened for new runs it can affect tie-breaking in NDCG/MRR. reproducibility checklist: fixed seed, deterministic sorting, same preprocess. :white_check_mark:
eval-bot: queued eval job 77821 for per-query-deltas (runtime estimate ~18m)
Marta: quick ad-hoc: run per-query delta and then compute: median_delta, pct_neg, top10_neg_sum. KS-test against baseline deltas helps. python snippet I toss around:```python
import json
from collections import defaultdict
base = {q['id']: q['score'] for q in json.load(open('base_scores.json'))}
new = {q['id']: q['score'] for q in json.load(open('new_scores.json'))}
deltas=[new[q]-base[q] for q in base if q in new]
# then use numpy.percentile/delta histogram
```
Marta: also log-rank differences: how many queries lost top-1 vs gained top-1. that is often more actionable than ndcg alone.
Ravi: to debug: 1) per-query deltas 2) sample 1k worst queries and inspect tokenization + truncation + candidate lengths 3) rerun a small reproducible batch with baseline model weights but new pipeline to isolate preprocessing.
Jules: +1. I'll start with step 1 and share CSV. @Marta can you run KS and top1-change counts when the CSV is up? :pray:
Marta: yup will do. also worth checking quantization: were we using 8-bit activation quant vs baseline fp16? subtle rank changes possible on near-ties.
Ivy: re: quantization — the int8 path we used has a known issue where softmax numerics differ slightly under long contexts. check logits variance across candidates, maybe renormalize before ranking as a quick probe.
Sam: small sanity: try eval on a slice of queries that are only short queries (<16 tokens). if they do better, it's a truncation/formatting issue. if they also drop, model change likely.
Jules: good plan. putting together the CSV and short/long split now. will upload to /shared/rerank/investigations/3701234567/per_query_deltas.csv when done.
Marta: once we have that CSV i'll run KS and also run a bootstrap CI on ndcg to see if drop is statistically significant for the holdout sample.
Ravi: let's avoid big re-training yet — want to ensure it's not eval harness or tokenization.
Jules: noted. quick note — found one suspicious thing: our prod candidate gather pipeline dedupes by doc id but new preprocess lowercases the query and doc contents earlier; dedupe now collapses a few near-duplicates differently. can add that to the checklist.
Ivy: good catch. dedupe change could shift candidate pools and produce systematic drop. re-run with dedupe disabled to isolate.
Sam: TL;DR action items: Jules run per-query CSV + short/long split (owner Jules), Marta run stats and top1-change (owner Marta), Ravi run harness parity test (owner Ravi), Ivy check quant and dedupe diffs (owner Ivy). update thread when you have CSVs. :rocket:
Jules: will update by EOD. thanks all :eyes:
